headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors when AutoGen writes code or files that Khoj indexes and reuses as conversational context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can write files and emit tool-driven outputs; Khoj reads indexed documents and personal notes. If AutoGen places attacker-controlled content into shared files, Khoj may ingest it as trusted context. This is not provably blocked by either profile, but the shared-file pathway is explicit.
conditions: IF AutoGen writes untrusted content into a directory Khoj indexes
IF Khoj treats indexed document text as instruction-bearing context
mitigations: Separate AutoGen working directories from Khoj indexed folders
Disable automatic indexing of AutoGen output directories
Add a manual review step before Khoj ingests new files
Prefix AutoGen outputs with machine-readable metadata only
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on indexed content

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen has broad network egress and can read/write filesystem contents; Khoj indexes personal notes and documents and also calls APIs. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive application data can flow from AutoGen into Khoj’s indexed corpus or outbound requests. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so the shared-workspace leakage path is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to access the same directory tree
IF AutoGen processes files containing sensitive application data
IF Khoj indexes those files or sends retrieved snippets to configured APIs
mitigations: Use separate directories for raw data and generated outputs
Exclude sensitive folders from Khoj indexing
Run AutoGen in a container with a narrow mount set
Review Khoj’s indexed sources before enabling chat
requires-engineering: add per-folder access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem while Khoj cannot write files, so direct write-write conflict is limited. A conflict still exists if both are pointed at the same mutable workspace and AutoGen overwrites files that Khoj reads or indexes. Because only one side writes, the blast radius is narrower than a full shared-write race.
conditions: IF AutoGen and Khoj share a mutable directory
IF Khoj indexes files that AutoGen may rewrite
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Make Khoj’s source folder read-only
Use timestamped output filenames from AutoGen
Pause indexing during AutoGen writes
requires-engineering: add file-lock coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code or structured outputs, and Khoj’s retrieval/chat flow can surface those outputs as context. If Khoj treats AutoGen-produced text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into later answers or actions. The profiles show a plausible A-to-B handoff, but no built-in verification step is documented.
conditions: IF AutoGen output is copied into Khoj notes or indexed documents
IF Khoj answers using retrieved AutoGen output without human verification
mitigations: Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted in filenames or headers
Require source citations before Khoj reuses retrieved text
Spot-check retrieved snippets before acting on them
Keep generated code out of long-term notes
requires-engineering: add verification gates for retrieved content

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and self-hostable, so there is no inherent residency or certification mismatch shown. However, AutoGen handles model provider API keys and broad egress, while Khoj indexes personal notes and may call cloud or self-hosted servers. Compliance risk appears only if regulated data is routed through a noncompliant deployment.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Khoj’s indexed notes
IF AutoGen forwards that data to a third-party model provider without a DPA
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of indexed corpora
Use self-hosted model endpoints for both agents
Review retention settings before enabling sync
Separate compliance-sensitive projects from general notes
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency controls
